answers.name: Great white shark
answers.fact: Called a white pointer in Australia.

answers.name: Hammerhead
answers.fact: Its wide head spreads out its electrical sensors.

answers.name: Tiger shark
answers.fact: Eats almost anything; licence plates have turned up in stomachs.

answers.name: Whale shark
answers.fact: The biggest fish in the sea, and a gentle filter feeder.

answers.name: Bull shark
answers.fact: Can swim far up rivers into fresh water.

answers.name: Mako
answers.fact: The fastest shark, at over 70 km/h.

answers.name: Megalodon
answers.fact: Extinct for about 3.6 million years, and up to around 15–18 m long.

answers.name: Basking shark
answers.fact: The second-biggest fish, filtering plankton with its mouth wide open.

answers.name: Blue shark
answers.fact: Makes some of the longest migrations of any shark.

answers.name: Nurse shark
answers.fact: Rests on the sea floor during the day.

answers.name: Lemon shark
answers.fact: Named for its yellowish skin.

answers.name: Blacktip reef shark
answers.fact: Common on tropical reefs.

answers.name: Whitetip reef shark
answers.fact: Hunts in reef crevices at night.

answers.name: Grey nurse shark
answers.fact: Looks fierce, but rarely bothers people.

answers.name: Wobbegong
answers.fact: A flat, camouflaged ambusher from Australian waters.

answers.name: Port Jackson shark
answers.fact: Has a pig-like snout and lays spiral-shaped eggs.

answers.name: Thresher shark
answers.fact: Stuns fish with its huge, whip-like tail.

answers.name: Goblin shark
answers.fact: Shoots its jaws forward to grab prey.

answers.name: Oceanic whitetip
answers.fact: A bold shark of the open ocean.

answers.name: Dogfish
answers.fact: Can live for 70 years or more.

answers.name: Angel shark
answers.fact: Flattened like a ray.

answers.name: Leopard shark
answers.fact: A spotty shark from California.

answers.name: Zebra shark
answers.fact: Striped when young, spotted when grown.

answers.name: Bronze whaler
answers.fact: A common shark around southern Australia.

answers.name: Gummy shark
answers.fact: Often sold as 'flake' in Aussie fish and chips.

answers.name: School shark
answers.fact: Also sold as flake.

answers.name: Frilled shark
answers.fact: A 'living fossil' with an eel-like body.

answers.name: Cookiecutter shark
answers.fact: Bites neat round plugs out of bigger animals.

answers.name: Megamouth
answers.fact: Only discovered in 1976.

answers.name: Six-gill shark
answers.fact: Most sharks have five gill slits; this one has six.

answers.name: Silky shark
answers.fact: Named for its smooth skin.

answers.name: Spinner shark
answers.fact: Spins as it leaps out of the water.

answers.name: Porbeagle
answers.fact: Can keep its body warmer than the water around it.

answers.name: Bonnethead
answers.fact: The only shark known to eat lots of seagrass.

answers.name: Epaulette shark
answers.fact: Can 'walk' on its fins between rock pools.

answers.name: Salmon shark
answers.fact: A warm-bodied shark of the cold North Pacific.

answers.name: Sleeper shark
answers.fact: A slow, deep-water giant.

answers.name: Horn shark
answers.fact: Has spines in front of its dorsal fins.

answers.name: Lanternshark
answers.fact: Some species glow in the dark.

answers.name: Pocket shark
answers.fact: Has a mysterious pocket near each front fin.

answers.name: Ninja lanternshark
answers.fact: Named in 2015, with help from some schoolkids.

answers.name: Pyjama shark
answers.fact: Striped like a set of PJs.

answers.name: Speartooth shark
answers.fact: A rare river shark of northern Australia.

answers.name: Greenland shark
answers.fact: May live for around 400 years, the longest of any vertebrate.
